thesis: Sincere repentance (with prayer and zakah) turns former enemies into brothers in religion, while renewed oath-breaking joined to attack on the deen exposes its perpetrators as leaders of kufr who must be confronted.

flags.quote: faqatilu a'immata al-kufr. Fight the leaders of disbelief.
flags.issue: Ahkam adab: qital command with explicit classical ikhtilaf never acknowledged. Al-Tabari records dispute over who a'immat al-kufr are (Qatadah/Mujahid/al-Suddi: named Quraysh leaders; Hudhayfah and Ali: 'the people of this ayah have not yet been fought'), and Qatadah's report condemns Khawarij-style misuse against ahl al-qiblah; Ibn Kathir derives the contested ruling on one who curses the Messenger. Zero ikhtilaf acknowledgment, no tadabbur-vs-fatwa distinction.

flags.quote: do I know how to recognize when corruption has become organized, oath-breaking, and aggressive enough that soft language is no longer truthful?
flags.issue: Generalizes the fighting command into a present-tense lesson about identifying 'leaders in corruption' today, universalizing a verse whose general applicability classical authorities disputed (Hudhayfah vs Ibn Kathir). Mitigating: file converts 'fight' into 'name/recognize'.

notes: Thesis solidly GROUNDED (al-Tabari: fa-ikhwanukum fi al-din = full brotherhood; a'immat al-kufr = ru'asa' al-kufr). All mechanical checks pass. Fix = ikhtilaf paragraph (who the a'immah are, Hudhayfah report, anti-Khawarij caveat) + tadabbur/fatwa line.

thesis: A spoken word of kufr remains real before Allah even when denied under oath afterward, yet the door of repentance is still held open before final turning away.

flags.quote: The command joins outward and inward enemies, then adds severity. There are times when firmness itself is part of mercy because moral boundaries must be defended from deliberate erosion.
flags.issue: Treats 'jahidi al-kuffara wa al-munafiqina' as one undifferentiated command, but al-Tabari opens with 'wa-khtalafa ahl al-ta'wil fi sifat al-jihad' — Ibn Mas'ud (hand/tongue/heart/stern face), Ibn Abbas/al-Dahhak (sword for kuffar, TONGUE for hypocrites), al-Hasan/Qatadah (hudud). Jalalayn + Muyassar: sword vs tongue-and-proof. The dominant classical readings deny uniform treatment; file flattens the famous ikhtilaf on the most contested word of the passage.

flags.quote: This is decisive. Human denial does not compete with divine witness.
flags.issue: Sound as tadabbur, but presented without the tadabbur-vs-fatwa line distinguishing moral reality before Allah from the legal handling of denial (the Prophet judged by outward profession; al-Julas's blood/property protected after retraction) — the very distinction the classical sources labor over on this ayah.

notes: Thesis GROUNDED (Ibn Kathir's al-Julas asbab carries the exact arc incl. sincere tawbah). Mechanical checks pass. Critical flag confined to the 9:73 jihad-mode ikhtilaf omission — one paragraph + a tadabbur/fatwa line fixes it without disturbing the thesis.
